newsitem.title: JAPAN: Supporters say concerned of Japan bishop's health.
newsitem.headline: Supporters say concerned of Japan bishop's health.

text.p: Supporters of an 80-year-old Japanese bishop detained in Malaysia after taking part in a conference on East Timor said they were worried about his health because of his age, the Sankei Shimbun reported on Sunday.
"He told us before he left that it was quite likely he would be arrested," Father Toyohiko Hirata of the catholic diocese of Nagoya, told the Japanese daily.
"He said if anything happened he would contact us, but there's been no word until now. We are afraid for his health because of his old age," he told the newspaper.
Bishop Nobuo Soma's diocese is in Nagoya, central Japan.
The bishop was one of the estimated 45 foreigners detained by Malaysian immigration officials on Saturday after a youth group allied to the Malaysian government broke up the conference on East Timor.
Another bishop. the Rev. Hilton Deakin of Melbourne, Australia, was also among those detained.
Soma led a delegation of four other Japanese, an Italian priest and an American translator to the Asia-Pacific Conference in East Timor.

Activists from some 18 non-governmental organisations had tried to hold the conference despite warnings by the Malaysian government that it would seek all legal means to halt it so that ties with neighbouring Indonesia would not be harmed.
Hundreds of members of the Malaysia Public Action Front loyal to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad interrupted the opening session of the conference.
In the ensuing struggle, Malaysian riot police moved in and detained the activists.
